title: AIDA implementation build record
description: What `build-record` verified for one attempt at one unit, at <task folder>/implementation/build-<unit_id>.json (docs/stages/implement/checks.md). One file per unit, holding only the latest attempt: a later attempt overwrites it. This record runs the three deciding checks: the order's own proof passes, the order's commits touch only files this order owns, and every frozen test file is unchanged. The tools run once at preconditions and again at review, so a tool row never spends an attempt. The model writes the code; this file is the script's own half, verifying what came back rather than judging whether a criterion is met. Plain JSON, no fences, no markdown. A field present in a real record but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field every other AIDA record carries.

takenAt.description: The UTC date this attempt was recorded, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script at the moment of writing, never typed by hand.

unit.description: The work order id this record belongs to, the same id `build-brief` was given and the file's own basename encodes (build-<unit_id>.json). Joined on, never re-minted.

startedAt.description: The commit this attempt began from, the full form of the `--started-at` value `build-record` was given, resolved and confirmed to name a real commit in the code repository (exit 43 otherwise). The list in `commits` is read from here to `commit`.

commit.description: The code repository's HEAD at the moment `build-record` ran, read fresh with `git rev-parse HEAD`, never assumed. Together with `attempt`, this is what exit 45 compares a new call against to refuse recording the same attempt twice.

commits.description: The commits the implementer made, full form, oldest first. `build-record` derives it: every commit from `startedAt` to `commit`, less each commit another order's records name, in a build or fix list or as a freeze. The owned-files check reads the files these commits change, and no range. `review-brief` builds the order's diff from this list, `commitsBefore` and the fix records' lists. A record without it was written before the lists, and each step that reads it reads its list from `startedAt` to `commit` the same way.

commitsBefore.description: Present after a second attempt, or after a person kept a stopped builder's commits: the commits the earlier attempts listed, which this file no longer holds, since it keeps the last attempt alone, and the commits from the last record, or the freeze, up to `startedAt` that no other order lists. The owned-files check reads the paths these change that still differ from the parent of the order's oldest commit to `commit`, so a stray change nobody reverted still stops the attempt, and one a later commit reverted does not. `review-brief` reads them, so every attempt is in the order's diff.

attempt.description: Which attempt at this unit this is, one more than the ledger's own attemptsUsed before this call. `build-record` increments attemptsUsed after writing this record, whether the checks below were met or not: an attempt is a dispatch that ended, not a dispatch that succeeded.

interfaceRecord.description: The text at the path `--interface` named, copied verbatim. The reviewer compares it with the unit's own declared interface, and the next orders' test briefs carry it. Required to be present and non-empty only when the unit's own frozen interface is non-empty (exit 44); otherwise this may be empty, including when no file was there to read.

interfaceRecordBefore.description: Present only after a re-check read an interface record whose text differs from the attempt's own: the text the attempt recorded, kept when a later re-check reads another. Review reads it beside interfaceRecord, so an amendment is compared with what the builder first wrote (gap row 253).

reportPath.description: Where the builder's own report lives, copied from `--report` as given. Only the path is kept here, never the report's content: docs/stages/implement/checks.md refuses the builder's account of what it did as authority, so this record never carries it as though it were evidence.

deviationAccepted.description: A deviation the builder declared that a person kept (gap row 266). A deviation line is a stop (exit 105). A person keeps it with `go-on --continue keep`, and `build-record` runs again and records the attempt: `departure` is the first deviation line, `file` the report or interface record that holds it, and `because` the person's words, read from deviationKept in the ledger. `stopsCleared` in the ledger records the same words, and `review-record` carries this object to the review record instead of stopping on the same line. Present only when a person kept one.

checks.description: The three deciding checks this step runs, in a fixed order: the order's own proof, owned-files, frozen-tests. Each carries its own verdict, so nothing downstream has to re-derive one from an exit code this file does not store on its own. No tool row runs here: preconditions runs each tool once, and review runs them over the whole task.

executed.description: How many of the checks in `checks` actually executed: they ran a command, which is every check carrying an exitCode, or they computed a diff or a hash, which is owned-files and frozen-tests. A frozen-tests row reading undeclared hashed no file, so it is not counted either: counting it would do the thing this field exists to stop. The field exists because a record saying every check answered, without saying how many of them ran, reads the same whether the code was tested or nothing was.

commitBefore.description: The record's commit before this run moved it to HEAD.

personFix.description: Present only after `go-on --continue check` ran the checks over commits of this order made after the record, such as the fix a person committed after a finding ruled load-bearing stopped the order (live-run row 426). The checks ran from `startedAt` to the new `commit`, so close reads a record at HEAD. A check that failed leaves the order stopped. The person's words are in the ledger's stopsCleared entry for that go-on, and the task record holds the warning.

recheckedAt.description: Present only after `go-on --continue check` ran the checks again over this record's own range, with no implementer dispatched and no attempt spent (live-run row 87): the UTC date of that run, YYYY-MM-DD. `checks`, `executed` and `decidingChecks` then hold that run's answers; `attempt`, `startedAt`, `commit` and `takenAt` stay the attempt's own.

checksBefore.description: Present with `recheckedAt`: the checks the second run replaced, id and verdict only, so a reader can see what it answered differently. The replaced outputs are not kept; the tool that refused a path printed nothing worth reading back.

decidingChecks.description: States plainly which of the deciding checks docs/stages/implement/checks.md names this step ran. All three of them; the field stays because a reader must never have to count `checks` to learn what a pass here covered.

total.description: The number of deciding checks docs/stages/implement/checks.md names in total. Always 3; a constant rather than a count of `checks`, so a step that ever ran fewer than all of them could not hide it.

ranHere.description: The `id` of each check in `checks`, in the same order, copied rather than re-derived, so a reader who only wants coverage never has to open `checks` to get it.

id.description: Which of the three checks this is. The first is the order's own proof, and its id names the proof kind. order-tests is 'Every test of this order passes'. configuration-gate takes that slot on an order whose proof is gate: the `## Configuration gate` lines of the implement recipe, run in the worktree, met when every line exits 0, unmet naming the first line that did not, unknown when the task records no environment, no implement recipe was passed, or the recipe carries no such block (live-run row 65). done-when takes it on an order whose proof is record: the judgement the checkpoint left on the order's ledger entry from its `--row <unit_id>=...`, met when confirmed, carrying `judgedBy` so close can copy the judge (nyc defect 17). observed takes it on an order whose proof is observe: the record the orchestrator wrote after a model looked at the page the order builds at one size, met when every row is met, carrying `judgedBy: model` (live-run row 104). confirm-at-review takes it on an order whose proof is confirm: it reads deferred, because a person confirms the order's done-when rows at review (gap row 196). owned-files and frozen-tests are 'The order's commits touch only files this order owns' and 'Every frozen test file is unchanged'.

verdict.description: The four words every verdict in this stage uses, and one more that only confirm-at-review carries. deferred means the task has no automated tests, and the person answers at review; it passes the floor. undeclared means no resolved recipe carried a command for this check, or the recipe declared that row absent, or this order froze no test file so frozen-tests had nothing to hash, so the row did not apply here; undeclared is never satisfied and never a pass. The order's own proof carries a floor the others do not: it must have run and answered met, so undeclared or unknown there stops the attempt whatever the rest said, because an order nothing executed never reaches checks-passed. unknown means the check ran but nothing here can decide from it: its output held the --nothing-ran marker, so a selected-nothing exit 0 proved nothing; or the command holds {paths} while this order declares no ownedFiles. Neither reads as met, and every unmet or unknown spends the attempt.

detail.description: Why this verdict, in plain words naming what was compared: an exit code, a set of file paths that did not match, or which marker or file could not be read.

framework.description: The framework this run belongs to, as project.json records it.

verdict.description: What this framework alone answered, before the verdicts were folded into the one above. deferred ranks above met in that fold: a suite one framework left to finish has not answered yet.

runs.description: One entry per framework, present only on order-tests, which runs once per framework the task resolved a test recipe for, because the build runs in one repository that is all of them at once. The check's own verdict is the worst of these, with undeclared ranking lowest so a framework that declared nothing never drags down one that ran and passed.

exitCode.description: What the check's own command exited with, present only on the order's own proof, and only when a command was actually supplied and run: the order's tests, its gate lines or its verify lines. Absent for owned-files and frozen-tests, which compare files rather than run a command, and absent for a check left undeclared.

output.description: What the command printed, standard output and standard error together, verbatim, present under the same condition as exitCode. Kept whole and unmodified so a person or a later step can see exactly what the --nothing-ran marker check itself saw.

judgedBy.description: Present only on done-when and observed. On done-when, who judged the order's done-when row at the checkpoint, copied from the ledger's own doneWhenJudgement so `close` writes the same judge on the criteria the order owns (nyc defect 17). On observed, always model: a model looked at the page, and the record says so (live-run row 104).
